The Pan Niger Delta Forum has called on the Inspector-General of Police and the Department of State Services to investigate the reported killings and attacks on supporters of the National Democratic Congress during a political rally in Delta State. The forum urged security agencies to identify and prosecute those who masterminded, sponsored or participated in the violence. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, condemned the violence at a recent political rally organised by the NDC in parts of Ughelli, Delta State. Igali said media reports indicated that some persons had lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. Consequently, the former ambassador to Norway, Sweden and Denmark urged the police, DSS and other relevant security agencies to conduct a comprehensive, impartial and thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. He said, “Arising from the foregoing, we strongly urge the police, DSS, working in concert with other relevant agencies within the national security architecture, to undertake a comprehensive, impartial and thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the reported violence at the Ughelli rally. The PANDEF chairman recalled that the organisation had warned only the previous week against political violence, intimidation and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South region. He said the region had historically demonstrated commendable traditions of political sportsmanship, tolerance and civility in the conduct of elections. gali expressed concern that the reported attack in Ughelli occurred barely days after the forum appealed to communities in the region to remain vigilant against political violence. 2027: Kebbi APC accuses ADC of sponsoring thugs First q’finalist emerges in Zenith Bank Delta Cup 2027: No political ambition worth bloodshed – Bamidele “There is absolutely no place in our democratic practice for such levels of violence, brutality and desperation for political power,” he said. The forum warned that any breakdown of law and order in the oil-producing region could have serious implications for Nigeria’s economic and national security, given its strategic importance to the country’s oil and gas revenues. It also called on the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to support the families of those reportedly killed and ensure that injured victims received adequate medical attention. PANDEF stressed that political competition must be guided by tolerance, respect for opposing views and peaceful participation. Background The appeal came barely 24 hours after the NDC vowed to resist alleged attempts to intimidate its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, out of the 2027 general election. The party had accused the Federal Government of allegedly sponsoring a campaign of violence and political persecution against its members. The National Chairman of the NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas, made the allegation at a world press conference in Abuja, where he claimed that repeated attacks on the party’s candidates, supporters and campaign activities across the country were part of a deliberate plot to weaken the opposition ahead of the elections. Cleopas cited incidents in Enugu, Delta, Lagos, Kano and Cross River states, where he claimed party members had been attacked, injured and killed, while campaign facilities and vehicles were destroyed. In Delta State, he recalled an August 13 attack on the convoy of the party’s governorship candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Kuse, Ughelli South Local Government Area, which reportedly left six members injured.chairman also expressed concern that even routine political meetings had allegedly become targets of violence.
